The pre-existing `json.rs` fmt drift is unrelated to my change (only `util.rs` was modified). All tests pass.

## Summary

**Root cause:** In multi-line mode, `Replacer::replace_all` extends the search subject past the searcher-reported match range (`range.end + MAX_LOOK_AHEAD`) to allow regex look-around to work. It then called the default `Matcher::replace_with_captures_at` (crates/matcher/src/lib.rs:941), which replaces every match in that extended subject *and copies all remaining bytes to the end of the subject into the output*. That look-ahead region content—which was never actually matched—leaked into the printed replacement, "expanding" what appeared to be matched.

**Fix** (crates/printer/src/util.rs, `Replacer::replace_all`): in multi-line mode, drive the replacement manually via `captures_iter_at`:
- stop iteration once a match begins at/after `range.end` (matches that end beyond the range are still permitted, since look-ahead may be needed to match content starting inside the range),
- after iteration, copy the unmatched tail only up to `range.end` instead of to the end of the extended subject.

Single-line mode keeps the original `replace_with_captures_at` path.

**Validation:** `regression::r2208` (this issue) and `regression::r2095` (same family, `--only-matching --replace --multiline`) now pass, and the full workspace test suite passes (274 integration tests incl. `--features pcre2`, plus all unit tests in grep-printer, grep-searcher, grep-regex, grep-matcher, etc.).
